description: Resolving anger, contempt and disputes promptly before they develop into deeper injury or hostile action.
name: Anger and reconciliation

description: Resisting anxious accumulation and attending to present responsibilities while trusting God's care for basic needs.
name: Anxiety and provision

description: Seeking help persistently and responding to another person's genuine need with what is good for them.
name: Ask, seek and knock

description: Treating the meek, grieving, merciful, persecuted and peacemakers as people to honor rather than exploit or dismiss.
name: The Beatitudes

description: Confronting the conversion of a place devoted to God into a marketplace and examining the authority claimed for that intervention.
name: Cleansing of the Temple

description: Rejecting religious or procedural excuses that cancel a person's responsibility to support and honor their parents.
name: Tradition and care for parents

description: Assessing actions that dissolve or evade marital obligations and expose another person to sexual betrayal.
name: Divorce and faithfulness

description: Handling small tasks and another person's property honestly because trustworthiness does not begin only when the stakes become large.
name: Faithful in little

description: Practicing self-denial honestly without manufacturing visible hardship to win admiration.
name: Fasting without display

description: Balancing the need for rest with compassion for a crowd and organizing available resources to meet practical needs.
name: Feeding the five thousand

description: Using leadership and authority for humble, practical service rather than expecting others to absorb all low-status work.
name: Jesus washes the disciples' feet

description: Extending forgiveness and hope amid unjust violence rather than answering abuse with contempt or revenge.
name: Forgiveness at the cross

description: Persistently asking for what is needed to provide hospitality or help and trusting that a good response serves the recipient.
name: A friend at midnight

description: Assessing trustworthy conduct by its observable fruits rather than impressive religious claims, appearances or asserted authority.
name: Recognizing fruit and false claims

description: Taking God's commands seriously in both practice and instruction rather than treating technical compliance as sufficient.
name: Fulfilling the Law

description: Remaining faithful under distress, acknowledging vulnerability to temptation and refusing retaliatory violence at a moment of threat.
name: Gethsemane and Jesus' arrest

description: Helping someone discreetly without turning their need into self-promotion or a performance for public approval.
name: Giving without display

description: Testing a proposed action by whether one would reasonably want to receive the same treatment from another person.
name: The Golden Rule

description: Giving practical and costly help to a person in danger across social boundaries instead of passing by or narrowing who counts as a neighbor.
name: Parable of the Good Samaritan

description: Protecting those entrusted to one's care and distinguishing sacrificial responsibility from theft, exploitation or abandonment when danger arrives.
name: The good shepherd

description: Refusing to dominate others or seek rank for its own sake and instead using responsibility to serve.
name: Greatness through service

description: Responding compassionately to an excluded person's need while taking seriously instructions governing what to disclose afterward.
name: Jesus heals a man with leprosy

description: Doing good and relieving a person's suffering on a rest day instead of using the Sabbath as an excuse to withhold help.
name: Healing on the Sabbath

description: Examining one's own faults before correcting others and using care in deciding how correction should be offered.
name: Judging and self-examination

description: Searching diligently for what is lost and rejoicing over a person's repentance and restoration.
name: Parable of the lost coin

description: Seeking and restoring a person who has gone astray rather than dismissing them as expendable.
name: Parable of the lost sheep

description: Seeking the good of hostile people and refusing to reserve care only for allies or people who repay it.
name: Love your enemies

description: Refusing deliberate lust and removing opportunities that lead to sexual betrayal or objectification.
name: Lust and adultery

description: Recognizing that a small beginning may grow into something that gives shelter and benefit to many.
name: Parable of the mustard seed

description: Choosing a demanding faithful course instead of following a popular or convenient path toward harm.
name: The narrow gate

description: Making mutual love the visible standard for conduct and the identifying mark of discipleship.
name: A new commandment to love

description: Persisting in seeking justice for a vulnerable person despite delay or indifference from those with power.
name: Parable of the persistent widow

description: Approaching one's own faults honestly instead of claiming moral superiority by comparing oneself with a despised person.
name: Parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector

description: Praying sincerely, honoring God's name and forgiving others rather than using religious language as a public performance.
name: Prayer and forgiveness

description: Welcoming a repentant person with mercy while resisting resentment when another person receives restoration.
name: Parable of the prodigal son

description: Distinguishing legitimate civic obligations from what belongs to God when a question is framed as a trap.
name: Render to Caesar

description: Responding to insult, coercion or demands without reflexive revenge and with willingness to give beyond what is demanded.
name: Retaliation and generosity

description: Rejecting covetous accumulation and the assumption that possessing more resources secures a meaningful or safe life.
name: Parable of the rich fool

description: Noticing and responding to a suffering neighbor instead of allowing comfort and wealth to conceal their need.
name: The rich man and Lazarus

description: Examining whether attachment to possessions prevents concrete generosity and willingness to follow Jesus.
name: The rich man seeking eternal life

description: Interpreting rest in light of human need rather than treating a rule as more important than the people it is meant to serve.
name: The Sabbath was made for people

description: Making good work useful and visible for the benefit of others and God's honor rather than hiding responsibility.
name: Salt and light

description: A broad foundation for actions involving love, mercy, truthful speech, enemies, possessions, prayer and putting Jesus' teaching into practice.
name: The Sermon on the Mount

description: Treating food, water, welcome, clothing, care and companionship for vulnerable people as consequential acts of service.
name: The sheep and the goats

description: Considering accountability and the future consequences of managing another person's resources amid a crisis of trust.
name: Parable of the shrewd manager

description: Considering whether distraction, pressure or love of wealth prevents received instruction from becoming durable action.
name: Parable of the sower

description: Using entrusted resources diligently and being accountable to their owner instead of neglecting the responsibility out of fear.
name: Parable of the talents

description: Rejecting shortcuts that misuse power, manipulate Scripture, test God or trade faithful worship for control and prestige.
name: Temptation in the wilderness

description: Preparing for an important responsibility before the need arrives instead of assuming someone else will provide readiness at the last moment.
name: Parable of the ten virgins

description: Reordering possessions and commitments when recognizing the surpassing worth of God's kingdom.
name: The hidden treasure and the pearl

description: Choosing priorities when wealth, ownership or material gain competes with faithfulness to God.
name: Treasure and two masters

description: Speaking plainly and truthfully without false promises, misleading assurances or appeals to God's authority to secure belief.
name: Truthful speech and oaths

description: Judging obedience by what someone actually does rather than by a willing-sounding promise they do not fulfill.
name: Parable of the two sons

description: Extending the mercy one has received instead of enforcing another person's smaller debt with cruelty.
name: Parable of the unforgiving servant

description: Connecting fruitful action with abiding in Jesus, keeping his commands and loving others through self-giving friendship.
name: The vine and the branches

description: Responding seriously to God's invitation rather than rejecting it through indifference, hostility or assumed entitlement.
name: Parable of the wedding feast

description: Welcoming children and removing barriers created by people who regard them as too unimportant to receive care.
name: Jesus welcomes children

description: Avoiding premature removal of suspected wrongdoers when the intervention would also harm those who should be protected.
name: Parable of the wheat and the weeds

description: Recognizing violent attempts to seize entrusted property and reject the owner's rightful claim to it.
name: Parable of the wicked tenants

description: Assessing generosity in light of a giver's actual means and sacrifice rather than comparing only visible totals.
name: The widow's offering

description: Putting heard instruction into practice and building on a sound foundation that survives foreseeable stress.
name: Wise and foolish builders

description: Engaging across social boundaries with truthful, respectful conversation and directing worship toward God in spirit and truth.
name: Jesus and the Samaritan woman

description: Resisting a condemning trap, examining one's own guilt and extending mercy while still calling a person away from wrongdoing.
name: The woman caught in adultery

description: Honoring agreed compensation and distinguishing harm to oneself from resentment at generosity shown to someone else.
name: Parable of the workers in the vineyard

description: Welcoming a despised person while connecting repentance to concrete generosity and repayment of what was wrongfully taken.
name: Zacchaeus
